description.narrative:
Projektet "Förbättra kommunala avfallshanteringstjänster i Nordmakedonien 2023-2027", genomfört av SKL är resultatet av en Sida-finansierad förstudie som genomfördes i Nordmakedonien mellan december 2020 och juni 2021 för att utforska alternativ för att stödja god förvaltning och hållbarhet utveckling.
Projektet syftar till att förbättra kommunala avfallshanteringstjänster i Nordmakedonien med sikte på full överensstämmelse med EU-standarder, och på så sätt förbättra miljömässig hållbarhet och livskvalitet för alla invånare.
SKL:s insats fokuserar på att bygga upp avfallsplaneringskapaciteten hos kommuner i en av de 5 nya avfallshanteringsregionerna, i syfte att sprida resultaten över hela landet. SKL syftar också till att underlätta samordning och kommunikation mellan kommunerna, Föreningen av enheter för kommunal självstyrelse (ZELS), ministeriet för miljö och fysisk planering och ministeriet för kommunal självstyrelse.
Projektgenomförande kommer att ske i tre faser eller komponenter, varav de två senare kommer att köras samtidigt:
1. SKL planerar att initialt samarbeta med ett antal pilotkommuner, deras allmännyttiga företag, förvaltning och invånare (6 kommuner i den kombinerade avfallshanteringsregionen Pelagonija och sydvästra) för att förbättra avfallshanteringsplaneringen och stärka deras förmåga att leverera inkluderande och hållbara avfallshanteringstjänster.
2. I samarbete med den makedonska sammanslutningen av lokala självstyrelser (ZELS), kommer SALAR att stärka kapaciteten hos en bredare grupp av kommuner att planera och leverera inkluderande och hållbara avfallshanteringstjänster i linje med EU:s krav och som en del av det regionala systemet. Denna komponent kommer också att arbeta med jämställdhetsintegrering i tillhandahållande av avfallshanteringstjänster.
3. Slutligen, genom samarbete med ministeriet för miljö och fysisk planering och ministeriet för lokal självstyrelse, kommer den att försöka förbättra samordningen mellan nationell och lokal nivå och öka nationella aktörers kapacitet att stödja lokala självstyrelser i genomförandet av EU standarder inom avfallsområdet.

The project "Improving municipal waste management services in North Macedonia 2023-2027", implemented by SALAR is the outcome of a Sida-funded pre-study carried out in North Macedonia between December 2020 and June 2021 to explore options for supporting good governance and sustainable development.
The project aims to improve municipal waste management services in North Macedonia with a view to full compliance with EU standards, thus improving environmental sustainability and quality of life for all inhabitants.
SALAR's intervention is focusing on building up the waste management planning capacity of municipalities in one of the 5 new waste management regions, with a view to disseminating the results countrywide. SALAR also aims to facilitate coordination and communication between the municipalities, the Association of Units of Local Self-Government (ZELS), the Ministry for Environment and Physical Planning and the Ministry for Local Self-Government.
Project implementation will take place in 3 phases or components, the latter two of which will run concurrently:
1. SALAR plans to initially work with a number of pilot municipalities, their public utilities, administration and inhabitants (6 municipalities in the combined Pelagonija and South-West waste management region) to improve waste management planning practices and strengthen their ability to deliver inclusive and sustainable waste management services.
2. Working with the Macedonian association of local self-governments (ZELS), SALAR will strengthen the capacity of a wider group of municipalities to plan and deliver inclusive and sustainable waste management services in line with EU requirements and as part of the regional system. This component will also work on gender-mainstreaming in waste management service provision.
3. Finally, through working with the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning and the Ministry for Local Self-Government, it will seek to improve coordination between the national and local level and increase national actors' capacity to support local self-governments in implementing EU standards in the waste area.

The overall goal to which the proposed project will contribute is to improve municipal waste management services in North Macedonia with a view to full compliance with EU standards, thus improving environmental sustainability and quality of life for all inhabitants.
At local level, the main focus will be to work with selected pilot municipalities, local utilities and inhabitants on planning and delivery of waste services in line with EU guidance and the new national legislation and strategic plan on waste.
At the level of local government as a whole, the project will work with ZELS to disseminate lessons learned to a wider group of municipalities and to integrate the gender perspective into local waste management policy and planning.
At national level, the project will work principally with the Ministry for Environment and Physical Planning and the Ministry for Local Self-Government to enhance multi-level dialogue and coordination in waste management and to promote inter-municipal cooperation among all municipalities in the pilot regions.
The main expected outcomes are:
1. Partner municipalities have improved waste management planning practices and strengthened their ability to deliver inclusive and sustainable waste management services.
2. Local self-governments have strengthened their capacities for more inclusive and sustainable waste management services and gender mainstreaming.
3. Functional multi-level dialogue and coordination contributes to more effective implementation of the legal framework.
The proposed project is structured into three main components:
1. Support to selected municipalities
2. Capacity development through the local government association
3. Multilevel dialogue and coordination

description.narrative:
Key results:
- Existing Regional Waste Management Plans have been operationalized into municipal waste management action plans, allowing municipalities to create a simple and functional framework for continuous and systematic improvement of waste collection services. Beyond the 6 pilot municipalities, an additional 9 municipalities in the region have also developed and adopted such plans, accounting for 80% of the region. This is the first time since the creation of the Regional Waste Management Plans nearly a decade ago that any substantive efforts at operationalization down to the municipal level have been made.
- Significant progress has been achieved in implementing the local waste management action plans in the 6 pilot municipalities. The project is now stepping up efforts at addressing capacity gaps through tailored trainings. Synergies with upcoming EBRD-supported work on capacity-building will further enhance results.
- Waste selection pilots have been initiated in 5 out of 6 targeted municipalities, which, if scaled up can end up significantly reducing waste that will go to landfill under the future regional system, thereby cutting costs to municipalities. The cost of waste selection is currently recovered via resale of waste fractions to private recycling centers.
- The municipality of Ohrid, a UNESCO natural and cultural heritage site, through facilitation by the project has secured external funding in the amount of 50,000 USD to prepare technical documentation for the closure of the old city landfill, which is nonstandard and threatens public health and the unique natural values of the area. This is a direct synergy with another Swedish-funded programme on municipal governance implemented by UNDP.
- The municipality of Prilep, a national leader in terms of waste selection and recycling, has been supported by the project to prepare a technical draft, to obtain external funding and initiate construction of a waste selection and processing facility. The benefit of this facility is to reduce the amount of waste that will go to landfill and lower the costs to end users. Other pilot municipalities have been invited as observers to the process, for the purpose of mutual learning and leading by example. It is not expected that this will jeopardize the feasibility of the regional system.
- A partner conference was held in April 2025, attended by key stakeholders in the waste management space, including donors, institutions, municipalities etc. The conference reviewed the state of play and provided an agreed list of priorities for broad dissemination, including a suggestion of key messages for communication on waste to ensure coherent messaging across donors, institutions and implementing partners. A donor coordination group on waste was inspired by the conference and has had two sessions since, where the key messages have been adopted by other donors for broader dissemination and unified communication on waste management.
Other results:
- The project has supported municipalities to develop communication plans and will support the process of implementation, ensuring that outreach is gender-sensitized and adapted to the needs of vulnerable and marginalized communities.
- A landfill fire prevention study has resulted in specific recommendations to municipalities which, if broadly disseminated can markedly reduce landfill fires and result in increased safety and lower environmental impact.
- The project conducted a recyclables market research, identifying potential alternative financing sources for different waste streams.
- A waste management training curriculum was prepared based on the methodology piloted in the 6 municipalities for national dissemination.
- A capacity development plan for the sector for waste at the Ministry for Environment and Physical Planning (MoEPP) was prepared by the project, and a process was initiated to set up a formal coordination and reporting structure on waste within MoEPP.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
